subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a separate assistant action-token search path, and what token containment, read-target policy, scope, and proof requirements should it use?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but workspace-wide Slack search with event-scoped credentials affects privacy, authorization, logging, and product semantics that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` in the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, read-target/privacy enforcement, least-privilege scopes, docs, tests, and redacted live Slack proof.

options.title: Consolidate Slack search design first
options.body: Define one Slack search contract covering RTS and any user-token search behavior before accepting an implementation branch.

options.title: Defer Slack workspace search
options.body: Keep the issue open but block implementation until maintainers are ready to own the token and privacy model.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` in the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, read-target/privacy enforcement, least-privilege scopes, docs, tests, and redacted live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent Slack assistant/action lifecycle history and authored the related maintainer close comment routing search back to this issue.
